paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God's promises don't depend on who's winning the war. Four kings flattened one people after another, and the five kings of Sodom's side ran like their shoes were on fire. But Abram, a man living near the Oaks of Mamre, wasn't shaken, because Melchizedek blessed him with these words: "Blessed be Abram by God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth" (Genesis 14:19). The One who made heaven and earth is the One standing behind Abram, and that's WHO you can lean on too.

Now look at what Abram does with his win. The king of Sodom says, "Give me the people, but take the goods for yourself" (Genesis 14:21), and Abram says no thanks, not even a thread. He tells him, "I have raised my hand to the LORD God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth" (Genesis 14:22). I think Abram wanted everybody to know where his blessing came from, and it wasn't from Sodom's pocket. Friend, when you let God be the one who provides, you don't need anybody else to take credit.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery today. Before the rescue was even over, Abram gave a tenth of everything to Melchizedek, a priest of God Most High (Genesis 14:18-20). He gave first, and he stayed free of the offer on the table. Ask yourself, baker: who gets the credit when something good happens in my life, and am I trusting the Creator of heaven and earth with it? The story isn't over, friend, because Abram's journey is just getting started.
